title: Cap. VI Arg. 5: Matt. 24; Rom. 11:5; Eph. 1:11 — elect salvation certain because God so acts
pass_a_gloss: Whence that of Matt. 24: So as to deceive, if it were possible, even the elect. And Rom. 11:5: A remnant according to election. And Eph. 1:11: Being predestinated according to the purpose of him who works all things after the counsel of his will. As regards God therefore the salvation of the elect is certain; because from the decree of election he has determined so to act in their hearts by wonderful ways that they may be led to faith and penitence, that they may remain in faith and newness of life, and at last die in the Lord.
pass_b_english: Hence Matt. 24 (to deceive, if possible, even the elect), Rom. 11:5 (a remnant according to election), and Eph. 1:11 (predestined according to the purpose of him who works all things by the counsel of his will). Quoad God, the elect's salvation is certain: from the election decree he has resolved so to work in their hearts that they are led to faith and penitence, remain in faith and newness of life, and at last die in the Lord.
source_text: Unde illud Matth. xxiv. Adeo ut seducant, si fieri posset, etiam electos. Et Rom. xi. 5. Reservatio secundum electionem. Et Ephes. i. 11. Cum essemus praedestinati secundum propositum ejus qui omnia efficit ex consilio voluntatis suae. Quoad Deum igitur certa est salus electorum; quia ex decreto electionis statuit miris modis ita agere in cordibus eorum ut perducantur ad fidem et paenitentiam, ut in fide et vitae novitate permaneant, ac tandem moriantur in Domino.
